doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Upcoming gigs and approaching the bass-drums duo
summary: Rowe notes Berklee and NEC dates and asks how to listen; Ali explains the bass-drums duo format.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Henry, I see you’re doing something coming up at Berklee?
And the New England Conservatory? Man. You guys, I just love to see the arc of a career like that. And that’s really great.

And I look forward to hearing you guys perform tomorrow night. I’m going to be fascinated to — I think if there’s a type of jazz that I really need to know more about personally I think it’s what you guys do. So I’m going to be watching and listening very intently. I’m trying to figure out the level of spontaneity and structure and all that, and how that works.

Well if you keep in mind that it’s bass and drums, that would like get you over the hump, you know what I mean? Keeping that in mind. Because it’s a lot different from a full quartet or a quintet or whatever. Or even a duo with drums and saxophone or a duo with bass and saxophone. You know, this is two rhythm instruments playing together. And of course Henry has taken over the melodic structures as well as playing rhythmically. And I’m doing the best I can with the melodic stuff, as a drummer. Yeah I’m doing the best I can with the melodic stuff, being a drummer, but I hear melodically. So I approach the drums in a very different way than most drummers.
